text:
maya: Heads-up: after kernel roll yesterday I'm seeing a 6-12ms median increase on tail-heavy traffic. spikes correlated with prefill-heavy sessions.

infra-bot: deploy at 10:03 UTC — runtime v2.7.3 (kernel selector changes).

leo: Can you attach a perf profile? Is it prefill or decode?

maya: Quick perf summary: prefill queue lengths dropped, decode queue spiked. KV hit-rate dropped ~18% during warmup window. Example log line: `kv_warmup_ms = 120` and `kernel_switches=3` for affected flows.

srinivasan: That suggests KV priming not firing for prefill-heavy flows. Did we change the prefill sizing heuristic in the kernel selector?

jana: I ran a short microbench: when prefill and decode share the same batcher, kernel selector keeps picking the larger GEMM path which has higher startup for small decode steps. Hypothesis: coupling prefill+decode causes kernel churn and KV cold misses.

leo: Proposal: split prefill and decode into separate queue shards with different token_budget targets and independent kernel affinity. e.g. prefill_token_budget=8, decode_token_budget=64, and per-phase kernel_hint.

maya: Also add a KV-priming grace window (200ms) for sessions that transition prefill->decode so the KV cache isn't evicted between phases.

srinivasan: Patch idea: add `phase` tag to requests (`phase: prefill|decode`) and make scheduler phase-aware. Pseudocode:
```
if phase == "prefill":
  budget = 8
  kernel_hint = "small-gemm"
else:
  budget = 64
  kernel_hint = "fast-decoder"
```

jana: We should gate this behind a canary and perf regression alerting. Add per-phase p50/p95 comparisons and KV-hit-rate monitors to the rollout. I'll extend the eval harness to replay 1h production traces.

leo: :thumbsup: I'll prototype queue separation in branch `prefill-splay-queue` and run a 50k-req sim. PR: http://git/internal/r/redwood/runtime/prefill-splay-queue/1234

maya: One more metric: track KV hit-rate per session_id and kernel-switch_count. If kernel_switch_count spikes, that's a red flag.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled to `eng-runtime-canary` at 14:00 UTC.

srinivasan: If the experiment looks good, follow-up: automatic fallback policy to older kernel selection when `kv_hit_rate` drops > 10% or latency regresses.

leo: Thanks — assigning tasks: @leo implement queue shards; @jana extend eval harness; @srinivasan add metrics & fallback rule; @maya observe canary and report p50/p95 per phase.
